newsitem.title: USA: Cargo carriers seek new U.S. gateways to Latam.
newsitem.headline: Cargo carriers seek new U.S. gateways to Latam.

text.p: Miami's cargo airlines will never abandon the city, but will likely seek additional U.S. gateway cities as the Miami International Airport reaches capacity, an expert predicted here Thursday.
"Miami (International Airport) cannot keep doubling its capacity every five years," said Robert Booth, president of Aviation Management Services.
Despite grumbling about rising costs, high crime and congestion, the cargo carriers will not leave Miami, Booth said. "Miami is too important for the carriers to just leave."
MIA has vital infrastructure for air cargo that is difficult to match elsewhere. Besdies its geographic advantage to Latin America, over 400 freight forwarders are located around the airport.
"The airlines will look at alternative gateways. Most of the cargo that comes through Miami is not final destination Miami," Booth said.

Many other U.S. airports, including Houston, New Orleans, Oralndo and Atlanta, have been trying to develop a bigger cargo business and woo carriers away from Miami. "Everybody is looking at Latin America, it is a huge growth market," Booth said.
